headline: Launch bottlenecks. Funding surges. Defense pivots.
deck: Small satellite operators scramble while funding flows into defense tech.

stories.head: SpaceX rideshare oversubscription leaves operators stranded
stories.body: Small satellite operators are facing a significant bottleneck as SpaceX's rideshare missions become oversubscribed, forcing many to reconsider their launch strategies. With alternatives limited, players like Astra and Rocket Lab may need to ramp up production to meet demand. The scramble for access highlights the fragility of relying on a single launch provider.
stories.soWhat: If SpaceX continues to dominate, we might see a wave of consolidation among smaller launch providers—survival of the fittest in the launch market.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M in Series C round
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully closed a $190 million Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company specializes in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, which is increasingly critical as military and commercial interests converge in space. This investment underscores the growing importance of space security in the defense sector.
stories.soWhat: With this kind of capital, True Anomaly is positioned to become a key player in the space security landscape—watch for potential partnerships with defense contractors.

stories.head: House approves $55.5B for Space Force operations
stories.body: The House Appropriations Committee has greenlit a $55.5 billion budget for the U.S. Space Force, emphasizing the need for competition in satellite communications. This funding is likely to accelerate various projects, including the tactical SDA constellation bid from Anduril and L3Harris. The increased budget reflects a growing recognition of space as a critical domain for national security.
stories.soWhat: This budget approval could lead to a flurry of contract opportunities—companies should be ready to pivot quickly to capture this funding.

watchlist.title: Watch for SpaceX's launch schedule adjustments
watchlist.body: With the rideshare bottleneck, SpaceX may need to adjust its launch schedule, impacting timelines for many small satellite operators.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on True Anomaly's partnerships
watchlist.body: True Anomaly's new funding could lead to strategic partnerships with larger defense contractors, reshaping the co-orbital security landscape.

watchlist.title: Impacts of Space Force budget on contractors
watchlist.body: The approved budget will likely influence contract awards in the coming months—companies should align their proposals accordingly.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser flight tests
watchlist.body: With the critical design review cleared, all eyes will be on Sierra Space's upcoming flight tests to validate its DoD variant.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
